issue.title: ledger-tools reads task_refresh with getCache({path}) / getCache(file), so note-level freshness intervals never apply in Obsidian
issue.description:
bob-ledger-tools (bob-plugins @ d4197f7): the freshness note-interval lookup reads frontmatter with `this.app.metadataCache.getCache({ path: key })` (plugins/bob-ledger-tools/main.js ~7322), and `refreshFreshnessForChangedFile` uses `getCache(file)` with a TFile (~7851). Obsidian's `MetadataCache.getCache(path: string)` takes a path string, so both calls look up a non-string key and return null. The per-note `task_refresh` override (docs/freshness.md §2, interval precedence) therefore never applies on the plugin side, while Rust `bob freshness` honors it. dash/rotten buckets and `bob freshness list` would then disagree for any note that sets `task_refresh`. The other plugins use `getFileCache(file)`. The test stub (scripts/test-ledger-tools-freshness.cjs ~648) accepts objects, so tests pass. It is latent today: no top-level vault note sets `task_refresh` yet. But the freshness research recommends one (for example 14 on sase.md), and the per-note READY cap design reuses this frontmatter-read pattern for `ready_cap`.

Found while researching the per-note READY cap (research:202610/per_note_ready_cap_crowded_notes__cld.md).

task_type_fields.impact: Any note that sets task_refresh gets the default interval in Obsidian (dash READY/NEW/ROTTEN, rotten.md, status bar) but its own interval in bob freshness, so the two review surfaces disagree. Latent until a note sets task_refresh.
task_type_fields.location: bob-plugins plugins/bob-ledger-tools/main.js note task_refresh lookup (~7322) and refreshFreshnessForChangedFile (~7851)
task_type_fields.repro: Add `task_refresh: 30` to a note's frontmatter whose Ready tasks were stamped 8–29 days ago. `bob freshness list` treats them as FRESH (note interval 30), but in Obsidian `api.freshness.bucket(task)` still returns "rotten" (default 7-day interval), so they drop out of dash READY and show in rotten.md. Code: main.js ~7322 `getCache({ path: key })` and ~7851 `getCache(file)`; the fix is `getCache(path)` / `getFileCache(file)`, plus a stub that only accepts strings.

issue.creation_reason: Found while studying the frontmatter-read pattern that a per-note READY cap would reuse; the plugin passes non-string keys to getCache, so the documented note-level override silently diverges from Rust.
